description: Conjunto de evaluación de calidad. Las preguntas usan vocabulario distinto al de los documentos (para medir recuperación semántica, no léxica). relevant_ids son los documentos correctos de knowledge_base.json.

cases.question: How can I adapt a big pretrained model to my own field without retraining all of its weights?
cases.reference_answer: Use LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation): freeze the pretrained weights and train small low-rank adapters. It adapts the model by updating under 1% of its parameters, so it fits on a single consumer GPU.

cases.question: Which number tells me how good a language model is at predicting text?
cases.reference_answer: Perplexity. It is the exponential of the average negative log-likelihood per token; lower perplexity means the model predicts real continuations better.

cases.question: My model scores great on the data I trained it with but fails on fresh inputs. Why?
cases.reference_answer: That is overfitting: the model memorized the training data instead of learning general patterns. Use regularization, dropout, more data, and watch validation loss with early stopping.

cases.question: How do computers grasp that two words mean similar things?
cases.reference_answer: Through embeddings: words and sentences are mapped to dense vectors where similar meanings are close together, so the model can compare texts by meaning rather than exact words.

cases.question: How can I get a model to answer using my own private documents?
cases.reference_answer: Use retrieval-augmented generation (RAG): retrieve the relevant documents from a memory and pass them to the model as context, so it answers from your knowledge without retraining.

cases.question: What techniques make a trained model smaller and faster to serve?
cases.reference_answer: Quantization (store weights at lower precision) and knowledge distillation (train a small student to imitate a large teacher) shrink the model and speed up inference with little quality loss.

cases.question: What mechanism lets modern language models connect distant parts of a sentence?
cases.reference_answer: Self-attention in transformers: every token attends to every other token, capturing long-range dependencies that recurrent models struggled with.

cases.question: Should I always just collect as much data as possible?
cases.reference_answer: Not necessarily. Data quality usually matters more than quantity: a smaller set of clean, relevant, well-labeled examples often beats a larger noisy one and trains faster.

cases.question: Can a model learn a new task from just a couple of examples shown to it?
cases.reference_answer: Yes, via few-shot or in-context learning: a pretrained model infers the task from a few examples placed in the prompt, with no weight updates.

cases.question: What kind of hardware makes neural network inference run fast?
cases.reference_answer: GPUs, because they run the underlying matrix multiplications in massively parallel fashion, making them far faster than CPUs for neural network workloads.
